prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1027; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured's vehicle and a third-party vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office. The driver is named on the policy and is confirmed as the operator at the time of loss.

Entry 2: Police report and two statements confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the time of impact. Photos taken at the scene show damage that is largely consistent with the impact described, though none of the photos capture the exact contact point. No independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 3: Reviewed the vehicle's prior repair records and found no earlier damage to the affected areas. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage, and the policy was in force on the loss date.

Entry 4: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of how the collision happened matched what was given in the first notice of loss and in the follow-up call. The claimant has described the event the same way in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Medical records were received documenting a back strain. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and the claimant has no known prior injury to the same body area.

Entry 6: Treatment followed a typical course of care, with visits tapering as the claimant's condition improved. The provider's notes are consistent with the stated recovery timeline. No gaps or unusual changes in the treatment pattern were noted.

Entry 7: Reserve reviewed in light of the medical course and the vehicle damage estimate. File remains open pending the final bills and the attorney's demand package.
